chunks: And from him, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I performed Tawaf but did not know whether I had performed six or seven circuits, so I performed another Tawaf.' He said, 'Why did you not start over (from one)?' I said, 'I had already performed Tawaf and departed.' He said, 'There is no blame on you.'

key_terms.اسْتَأْنَفْتَ: Did you start over (from the beginning)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: There is no blame/damages on you

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I am unsure whether I completed 6 or 7 Tawaf circuits?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-istinaf* (starting anew) versus *al-ibtida'* (beginning fresh) in cases of doubt (*shakk*) during ritual worship. The Imam’s instruction highlights the Shia juristic preference for caution in ritual purity and completeness, yet the final ruling demonstrates the leniency applied when the worshipper has already concluded and departed the sacred precincts. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how uncertainty is resolved in the performance of *Tawaf* without imposing undue hardship on the believer.
